topic: Using std::copy with inserter and iterators for container manipulation
explanation: In modern C++, the combination of the std::copy algorithm with inserters and iterators allows for flexible and efficient transfer of elements between containers. This approach leverages iterator adaptors like std::inserter to insert elements into a container at a specified position, enabling seamless and expressive container modifications without manual loops. It exemplifies the power of the Standard Template Library (STL) algorithms and iterator abstractions to write concise, generic, and safe code.
syntax:
std::copy(InputIterator first, InputIterator last, OutputIterator d); // copies elements from [first, last) to destination
std::inserter(Container& c, Iterator pos); // creates an output iterator that inserts elements into container c starting at position pos
example_explanation: This example demonstrates copying all elements from a vector 'coll' into a list 'coll2' using std::copy combined with std::inserter. The inserter inserts the copied elements starting immediately after the first element of 'coll2'. The print function then displays the resulting list, showing how STL algorithms and inserters facilitate flexible container modifications in modern C++.
